content.text:
I submitted a portfolio, but it failed the validation check: its 1970–1999 training Sharpe is 4.07, and the sealed 2000–2012 verdict came back FAIL. That 4.07 is fitted on the same data it's measured on, so it overstates what to expect. A fairer guide is the forward-walk test on training data, which averaged about 0.95 out of sample.

I used only 1 of the 200 backtest calls, on purpose. I picked the method using training data only, by comparing approaches on later periods they hadn't seen. After the FAIL, I submitted the same portfolio rather than adjusting it against the PASS/FAIL verdict. Tweaking until something passes would really be fitting to the validation data, and would likely give a worse true validation Sharpe.

Final portfolio: it holds all 423 signals with mean-variance weights fitted on 1970–1999, with the covariance matrix blended 50/50 with its own diagonal to stabilise the weights, and weights scaled so their absolute values sum to 1. Most of its tilt comes from going long a few strong industries (such as Fun, Meals and Chips) and running most short-term trend signals in reverse; in training those trend signals consistently lost money, likely from trading costs or short-term reversal.
